### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa00ebf44759b7fcfb0a1e9f55256265068399a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `260feffb77bdc9f5259da62bd3bf85ebd2a13bdc` — the merge of head `d14811988009df1869d3660cc2d3e26d8e075e72` into base `fa00ebf44759b7fcfb0a1e9f55256265068399a8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 260feffb77bdc9f5259da62bd3bf85ebd2a13bdc && git checkout 260feffb77bdc9f5259da62bd3bf85ebd2a13bdc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fa00ebf44759b7fcfb0a1e9f55256265068399a8 d14811988009df1869d3660cc2d3e26d8e075e72 && git checkout -B drift-repro fa00ebf44759b7fcfb0a1e9f55256265068399a8 && git merge --no-ff d14811988009df1869d3660cc2d3e26d8e075e72

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fa00ebf44759b7fcfb0a1e9f55256265068399a8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d14811988009df1869d3660cc2d3e26d8e075e72`

Scope: 4 files (+232/−13) on merge base `aa04ea2964`:
- the `$between` arm of `TursoDriver.toRemoteFieldSpec`;
- the `$between` arm of `RemoteTransport.unsupportedOperator`, with its doc paragraph;
- the seam pin `remote-transport-compile-refusal-seam.test.ts`;
- the changeset.

No governed surface is touched.

Read: card #20094 with its triage, unlock and claim, #20039, PR #20093 and its record 5826632400, the PR body, the diff, all check-runs, AGENTS.md, `contract-review.md`, and the code at head and base.

Measured in two detached worktrees (head and base), each with `driver-turso`'s closure built. The probe drove a real remote `TursoDriver` over the in-repo libSQL stub beside `TursoDriver(':memory:')`, and it also drove `RemoteTransport` directly with a stub client and a diagnostic sink.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Every malformed shape: the premise is REAL at base and closed at head.** The seven shapes were `[x]`, `[x,y,z]`, a number, a string, `null`, `{}` and `[]`. Each ran under 3 marks through `find` and `count` on both faces: 84 cells per tree.
  - Base remote, 42/42: a plain `Error` with `code` and `status` undefined. It names `'object.field'` in 42/42 and echoes the comparand in 24/24 literal cells, logs nothing, and is the same for every caller.
  - Head remote, 42/42: `INVALID_FILTER` / 400, with own keys exactly `code,status`. The field appears in 0/42 messages and the comparand in 0/24. There is exactly one `warn` line with the field and comparand, and 0 statements execute.
  - The head remote non-author message equals `[RemoteTransport] ` plus the local class statement in 28/28 cells.
  - Local control: 42/42 cells are byte-identical at base and head.
  - `aggregate`, `updateMany` and `deleteMany` with `[x]` also answer `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 at head, with no row changed.
- **The refused set does not move: RIGHT.** 17 nested and multi-operator shapes × {unmarked, `'policy'`} × 2 faces = 68 cells, 0 moved. Well-formed shapes answer the same rows at base and head.
- **Well-formed ranges lower byte-identically: RIGHT.** Six controls: a numeric range, bare days on a `date` field, bare days on a `datetime` field (the whole-day upper bound of framework#4081), instants, a range under `$not` and a range inside `$or`. The lowered filter, the executed SQL and args, the rows and the counts are identical at base and head in 6/6, and remote equals local in 6/6.
- **The pins discriminate: RIGHT, and both claimed counts reproduce.** The seam pin passes 130/130 at head. With `turso-driver.ts` at its base blob it gives 28 failed / 102 passed; with `remote-transport.ts` at its base blob, 18 failed / 112 passed. Each file was restored by blob.
- **No `throw` remains in the remote lowering at head.** The removed wording has no reader in the repository.
- **Public surface: RIGHT.** Both changed methods are `private`. No export, `index.ts`, `package.json` or `packages/spec` file moves.
- **Existing pins:** `turso-remote-temporal-conformance.test.ts` passes 67/67 at head.
- **CI at this head:** 34 runs, 31 `success`, 3 `skipped`, 0 failures, and all seven required contexts are `success`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/driver-turso: patch`, `Clause-②: no`: RIGHT.
- The refused set is unchanged in 152 of 152 cells, and the rows are unchanged in every well-formed control.
- No export or signature moves. Message text is outside the published accept set (the #8197, #20037 and #20093 precedents).
- The declared fail-closed cost for a remote `'author'` caller narrows nothing that caller could rely on. At base it got a bare `Error` with no code; at head it gets `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. No remote transport refusal has disclosed to an author since PR #20093 (author equals unmarked in 14/14 cells).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Changeset: every sentence is TRUE.** The read-scope clause is measured through a `'policy'`-marked `where`, not through the plugin itself.
- **PR body: no FALSE sentence.** H1–H4, the 96 → 130 case count, both ablations and the acceptance notes reproduce. The whole-suite count and the gate families were not re-measured here; CI carries them.
- **The dev's deviations are answered.**
  - Not extending the text-parity file is correct: it has 0 `$between` rows.
  - Omitting the tracker id from the new runtime string is justified by the prose-id baseline.
  - The remote author cost is accepted per ②.
  - The three out-of-scope observations are correctly left unfiled.
